verdict.line: You lose if you let her free-hit with Q (Precision Protocol) autos off E (Hookshot) resets without ever being punished; you win if you force all-ins before level 6 while you hold 4-5 passive stacks and she doesn't.

brief.thesis: Darius wins this lane in the trade window, not the poke window: he has the lane and solo-kill edge (49.2% over 642 games) because his stacked passive and W execute threat beat Camille in prolonged melee, but her E (Hookshot) lets her hop to a wall, poke with an empowered Q auto, and disengage before he can punish. The whole matchup is about closing that gap between her hop and her landing.

theirWindow.when: she hops E onto a nearby wall
theirWindow.what: She's committed to a fixed landing spot and about to chain a second dash with an empowered Q auto attached. This is her only safe poke — she cannot flash out of the animation.

yourWindow.when: her E lands but before her second dash fires
yourWindow.what: Throw E (Apprehend) the instant she touches down to pull her into melee range before the chain completes — this negates her disengage and traps her in your zone for a full W into Q trade.

start.why: 82.1% pick rate for a reason — the lifesteal and AD keep you ahead in the extended trades that actually win this lane (49.8% WR, 625 games).

boots.why: 76% pick, 51.3% WR — Camille's damage is entirely auto-attack and Q-empowered autos, so flat physical reduction blunts her only poke tool.

core.why: The haste closes the mobility gap her E gives her — this is what lets you actually catch a Camille who wants to hop and reset neutral.
Free stacking movement speed on a wave push means you're never a full E-hop away when she tries to disengage.
65.2% WR over 66 games on this exact path — the damage-over-time conversion neutralizes her burst windows and keeps you alive through her all-in.

situational.when: the enemy team stacks magic damage around her
you need burst mitigation more than the healing from Death's Dance
you're duel-focused and need to run down a kiting Camille instead of executing squishies

runes.keystoneWhy: Camille wants short poke trades and disengage — Conqueror rewards you for forcing the fight to run long, which is exactly where Darius wins.

summoners.why: 71.1% pick rate — Ghost specifically lets you stay attached through her E hops, since her entire kit is built to create distance you otherwise can't close.

playing.title: Track her E cooldown constantly
playing.detail: When Hookshot is down, she has zero disengage — walk up and force trades freely, since this is the only window where she can't punish and run.

playing.title: Fight only at max passive stacks
playing.detail: Hold your Q (Decimate) hits until Hemorrhage is at 4-5 stacks before committing to a full trade — the true damage bonus is what actually wins the extended fight.

playing.title: Interrupt her E with your E
playing.detail: The moment she lands her first Hookshot hop, throw Apprehend to pull her into melee before the second dash fires — this is the single highest-value play in the matchup.

playing.title: Hit Q at the blade's edge
playing.detail: Decimate deals bonus damage at max range, not center — position so the rim of the circle lands on her, not just the tick near your feet.

playing.title: Never extend below 50% HP after level 6
playing.detail: Her ultimate isolates you in a zone she controls — once she has R, don't trade past half health or you're forcing a duel on her terms.

playing.title: Punish her poke with W
playing.detail: Every time she lands a Q-empowered auto and disengages, chase with Crippling Strike to slow and reset your passive stacks before she resets neutral.

playing.title: All-in the moment Ghostblade completes
playing.detail: The active haste is your one item spike that closes her mobility gap outright — look for a skirmish immediately after finishing it.

brief.patchCaveat: Build order, boots, runes, summoner spells, and every win rate here are measured OP.GG data from live games on the current patch; the timing windows, trade sequencing, and E-interrupt read are my own mechanical analysis.
